correctness.rationale: The smooth hypersurface dual-degree formula is the classical class formula d(d-1)^n. The tangent-normal sequence gives c(TX)=(1+H)^(n+2)/(1+dH), and Gauss-Bonnet gives the independently replayed Euler formula. Writing q=d-1, even and odd n yield explicit expressions for the difference between dual degree and absolute Euler characteristic. For q>=2 both are strictly positive; q=1 gives the complete quadric exception list. The bundled exact-arithmetic checker independently reconstructs the Chern-series coefficient and verifies the comparison over a broad finite grid.

value.rationale: Dual degree measures generic tangent-hyperplane complexity, while Euler characteristic is the most basic global topological invariant of the same hypersurface. The theorem gives a complete all-dimensional phase diagram between them: one equality object, one exceptional geometric family with reverse ordering, and universal domination from degree three onward. The statement is natural, uniform, and structurally interpretable rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
